newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends weaker on ideas market overbought.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends weaker on ideas market overbought.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures erased their earlier gains and ended mostly lower on ideas the market had been overbought and on spillover weakness from CBOT soybeans, traders said.
"The markets are tired. I think there was the feeling that we overdid the bull move yesterday in wheat," a trader said.

KCBT March wheat had been firm throughout the session on bullish export data and on strong follow-through buying by Rosenthal Collins. Rosenthal, a commission house with large fund interests, bought two million March bushels Thursday on top of the two million it bought Wednesday, traders said.
But March wheat was pressured late by spillover from CBOT soybeans, which dropped in response to crop production estimates included in President Clinton's proposed budget.

New crop July and September contracts eased as much-needed snows fell in the the central and southern U.S. Plains. Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said three to five inches of snow could fall across the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles and western Kansas.
KCBT wheat settled 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 1/2 cent higher, with March down 1-1/2 cents at $4.14. Earlier, March set an intraday high at $4.19, up 3-1/2 cents.
